title: Build the toy first, then the game.
author: StaticAnchor
selftext:
Hey all,

Just wanted to share my perspective as someone who's been in the product design/UX design field for over 10+ years.

Like most of you, I grew up fascinated with games. I never thought in my life I'd have the ability to create something playable, let alone fun.

I've seen posts here and across social media getting hyped up about "one shotting" games. While technically impressive, there is nothing that keeps me engaged.

My take - start small and build a toy first. Take that small seed of some kind of mechanic and naturally build around that. Let the inspiration of what you already like take over and guide you into what feels fun. Find the fun first, and then water it.

As a product designer, I often didn't get it right on the first shot, especially when first starting. The UX process teaches us about feedback and iteration. Even if you are shy about your own game, get lost in it and play it! What is lighting you up? What isn't working? Don't grip onto mechanics too tightly, and follow the path of what is making you smile.

There's a great video called [Everything is a Remix](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X9RYuvPCQUA) that talks about just how creation is made. We are always coming up with variations of things in our mind, AI just becomes an amplifier to our judgement and taste. An interview with Rick Rubin comes to mind. He can't play an instrument, he can't work a soundboard, but people seek him out because of the confidence in his taste and knows what feels good and what doesn't.

We are entering a wave where execution is now cheap. I encourage everyone to find a hook, a beat, a seed of something that's interesting, and figure out how you can expand on that.

It's how a came up with Soul Roll, a pinball roguelite heavily inspired by one of my favorite games of all time, Balatro. My mind kept telling me that there was something about Balatro's mechanics that overlapped with pinball. Player agency, elements of luck. Last year, I spent time learning Godot and building and early prototype. I understand the traditional route of developing a game, it's actually quite fun to figure something out and get it working. As the game fleshed out, I found certain mechanics didn't work. As someone who was slow in development, it could take me a week just to try something out that I went, nah that doesn't work.

Opus 5.5 was a game changer to me, cause it allows me to experiment and fail fast. Even the version you are seeing now, is no where near a complete game. But it's what we call in design "an MVP" and enough there for people to start to get a sense of what this is about.

In classic UX fashion, I'd love your feedback. The good, the bad, the ugly. You can play it on desktop or mobile (I'm biased but mobile is a total time sink lol).

I'm looking to drop a new prototype weekly just to show everyone what's possible when we build the toy first, and then the game.

Play Soul Roll for free: [https://hookandsinkergames.itch.io/soulroll](https://hookandsinkergames.itch.io/soulroll)  
Trailer: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9vGEMJZanGc](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9vGEMJZanGc)
